messages.subject: Alternate Parts and Density Covariates
parts:
Hello,

I am interested in linking sigma with density. I have a large dataset (2,500 animals) covering a large density gradient and many sessions (49). The sigma and a0 or c methods detailed in https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/secr-parameterisations.pdf seem like a good fit for  my work.

I am curious why this only works when D~session, but not when D~mask covariate. If, for example, D~mask covariate produces a better model, shouldn’t this produce better density, and sigma estimates for each session? Clearly there is some structural reason why this doesn’t work at the moment, but Im not sure why.



EX:

library(secr)

##make mask
clippedmask <- make.mask(traps(ovenCH), type = 'trapbuffer', buffer = 300, spacing=20)

##add fake mask covariates
for (i in 1:length(clippedmask)){
  covariates(clippedmask[[i]]) <- data.frame(rand = runif(1850, -2.0, 2))
}

##model from https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/secr-parameterisations.pdf
oven0509bs <- secr.fit(ovenCH, mask=clippedmask, model = list(D ~ session, sigmak ~ 1,
                                            a0 ~ bk), buffer = 300, detectfn = 'HHN', trace = FALSE)


##with density covariate
oven0509dc <- secr.fit(ovenCH, mask=clippedmask, model = list(D ~ rand, sigmak ~ 1,
                                                              a0 ~ bk), buffer = 300, detectfn = 'HHN', trace = FALSE)

###Error in secr.fit(ovenCH, mask = clippedmask, model = list(D ~ rand, sigmak ~  : 
##only session and group models allowed for density when details$param = 5

Thanks!

--
Clayton Lamb, PhD Candidate

Biological Sciences, University of Alberta

messages.subject: Re: Alternate Parts and Density Covariates
parts:
I'm not remembering all the details, but -
What you are suggesting implicitly makes sigma a function of the mask covariates, when sigma is generally fixed across the mask. We used a workaround for spatially determined density-dependent sigma in a possum example in the Ecography paper - using x and y as predictors (not sure about other covariates, but I think they work). See Appendix 3 in the online appendix.
Murray

Awesome, thanks Murray. Removing the multi-cores fixed the problem for OPT1. I’ll paste a working, reproducible script of this below, which builds on the OvenCH example I used to start this thread.

I wasn’t able to get Opt2 working.

library(secr)

##make mask
clippedmask <- make.mask(traps(ovenCH), type = 'trapbuffer', buffer = 300, spacing=20)

##add fake mask covariates
for (i in 1:length(clippedmask)){
  covariates(clippedmask[[i]]) <- data.frame(rand = runif(1850, -2.0, 2))
}

##model from https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/secr-parameterisations.pdf
oven0509bs <- secr.fit(ovenCH, mask=clippedmask, model = list(D ~ session, sigmak ~ 1,

a0 ~ bk), buffer = 300, detectfn = 'HHN')



###WORKING EXAMPLE TO LINK SIGMA WITH DENSITY PREDICTED FROM MASK COVARIATES ALONE

##Define function for non-euclidian distance
##from http://www.ecography.org/sites/ecography.org/files/appendix/ecog-01511.pdf
## Option 1: integrating along least-cost path
userdist1 <- function (xy1, xy2, mask) {
  if (missing(xy1)) return(c("D", "noneuc"))
  D <- covariates(mask)$D
  k <- covariates(mask)$noneuc ## noneuc = k
  sigma <- k / sqrt(D)
  if (!require(gdistance))
    stop ('install package gdistance to use this function')
  ## make raster from mask, assigning 1/sigma to all habitat cells
  Draster <- raster(mask, values = 1/sigma)
  ## Assume animals can traverse gaps: bridge gaps using mean
  Draster[is.na(Draster[])] <- mean(Draster[], na.rm = TRUE)
  ## form gdistance ‘TransitionLayer’ to define cell-cell connections
  trfn <- function(x) 1 / mean(x)
  tr <- transition(Draster, transitionFunction = trfn, directions = 16)
  tr <- geoCorrection(tr, type = "c", multpl = FALSE)
  ## costDistance finds length of least-cost path
  distmat <- costDistance(tr, as.matrix(xy1), as.matrix(xy2))
  distmat[!is.finite(distmat)] <- 1e10 ## avoid infinite values
  distmat
}


o1 <- secr.fit(ovenCH, mask=clippedmask,model = list(D~rand, noneuc ~ 1), detectfn = 'HHN', details =list(userdist = userdist1), link =
list(noneuc = 'log'), fixed=list(sigma=1))

## plotting
addSigma <- function (Dsurface, Dcovariate = 'D.0', k) {
  D <- covariates(Dsurface)[,Dcovariate]
  covariates(Dsurface)[,'sigma'] <- k / sqrt(D)
  Dsurface
}
DS <- predictDsurface(o1)
DS <- addSigma(DS[[1]], k = predict(o1)[[1]]$estimate[3] )

plot(covariates(DS)$D.0, covariates(DS)$sigma)





###NOT WORKING YET

## Option 2: averaging density-dependent sigma at endpoints of path
userdist2 <- function (xy1, xy2, mask) {
  ## use addCovariates here to associate D with each point
  xy1 <- addCovariates(xy1, mask)
  xy2 <- addCovariates(xy2, mask)
  D1 <- covariates(xy1)$D^0.5
  D2 <- covariates(xy2)$D^0.5
  k <- covariates(mask)$noneuc[1] ## assume k constant
  euc <- edist(xy1, xy2)
  sig <- outer (D1, D2, FUN=function(d1,d2) k * (1/d1 + 1/d2)/2)
  euc / sig
}


o2 <- secr.fit(ovenCH, mask=clippedmask,model = list(D~rand, noneuc ~ 1), detectfn = 'HHN', details =list(userdist = userdist2), link =
list(noneuc = 'log'), fixed=list(sigma=1))

  distmat <- costDistance(tr, as.matrix(xy1), as.matrix(xy2))

}

  euc / sig
